custom_logic_notes: The EA implements a custom support/resistance detector by scanning price levels in 0.001 increments from the bar low to high over a configurable period (default 500 bars, 100 for XAUUSD), counting how many bar closes match each level. If a level has more hits than the 'resistance' input (default 15) and is within 0.0005 of current ask/bid, it is considered a resistance/support zone. Buy enters when ask is above this resistance zone; Sell enters when bid is below this support zone. The 0.001 step size and 0.0005 proximity threshold are hardcoded and may not suit all instruments (especially JPY pairs or XAUUSD). Volatility calculation via MathVariance exists but is unused (a polynomial resistance formula is commented out). The Buy order uses magic number 15489 (hardcoded, ignoring EA_Magic input), while Sell uses the EA_Magic input — this is likely a bug. Margin check is present but the margin variable is never populated by OrderCalcMargin, so the check margin<free_margin is unreliable.
python_conversion_notes: 1. The custom resistance detection loop iterates from min to max close in 0.001 steps — this is extremely slow and must be replaced with a proper histogram/bin approach in Python. 2. MathVariance from Normal.mqh is equivalent to numpy.var(ddof=0). 3. The hardcoded 0.0005 proximity threshold is instrument-specific and won't work for XAUUSD or JPY pairs — needs to be parameterized using _Point or ATR. 4. The 0.001 step in the resistance scan loop is also instrument-specific. 5. Magic number inconsistency (Buy=15489, Sell=EA_Magic) should be flagged or fixed. 6. Margin check is broken (margin variable uninitialized) — must implement proper margin calculation or remove. 7. The PositionSelect check only works for single-position per symbol (netting accounts) — hedging accounts would need PositionSelectByTicket or iteration. 8. The period variable (500/100 for XAUUSD) should be an input parameter. 9. Current bar [0] MA values are used for entry signals — in Python backtesting this means same-bar lookahead unless shifted to [1].
